description: Teknoİlke is a student team building ASTRA, an offline-first health monitoring prototype for long-duration space missions. Designed for low-connectivity environments, ASTRA tracks vital signs and highlights missing medical data using strict, evidence-based logic. We’re looking for passionate minds in Python, UI/UX, data science, biology, and aerospace to join us. Build carefully, work with evidence, and help shape the future of space health.
summary: ASTRA is an offline-first research and demonstration workspace for astronaut health monitoring. It keeps three evidence types separate: NASA OSDR OSD-575 transformed serum-assay data for retrospective biomarker exploration; synthetic or manually entered vital-sign readings for local demonstrations; and a reproducible 30-day mission replay with a browser-based experimental machine-learning pattern screen. Before displaying NASA-derived measurements, ASTRA checks the preserved source file, its SHA-256 fingerprint, the sample-to-metadata mapping and nine-analyte normalization. A seven-day data-quality gate preserves missing values and blocks model inference when telemetry coverage is insufficient. Core application assets, the local model and NASA source files are cached for offline use after an initial online load. The prototype demonstrates evidence-aware review in constrained environments. OSD-575 is a small retrospective biospecimen study, while the model was trained and evaluated only on generated synthetic data. ASTRA is not a validated medical device or an official NASA product.
details:
ASTRA is a browser-based, offline-first research and demonstration workspace developed for astronaut health monitoring. It is organized into three distinct modes so that historical NASA research, simulated telemetry and manually entered readings are never presented as the same type of evidence.

NASA Research Mode uses the NASA Open Science Data Repository's OSD-575 Version 3 HDCVD9 transformed serum-assay dataset and its associated ISA sample metadata. Before displaying biomarker profiles, ASTRA checks the preserved source file against a project-maintained SHA-256 fingerprint, verifies the one-to-one mapping of 28 samples to the NASA metadata, checks participant and collection-timepoint coverage, and audits the normalization of nine analytes. The dataset represents four independent participants and repeated retrospective serum samples. It is not a continuous heart-rate, blood-oxygen or temperature feed.

Demo & Manual Mode provides a separate interface for simulated or manually entered heart rate, SpO₂, body temperature and sleep-duration readings. It includes input validation, configurable demonstration reference bands, a locally captured reference snapshot and a separate wellbeing self-report. These values are not attributed to NASA research observations.

Mission Replay provides seven reproducible, fictional 30-day telemetry scenarios. ASTRA's experimental MLP runs locally in the browser and evaluates a rolling seven-day feature window. Before inference, a deterministic data-quality gate checks signal completeness. It requires at least five of seven daily readings for each vital-sign channel and at least five of seven fatigue and stress self-reports. If the evidence is insufficient, ASTRA abstains, displays no model score and leaves missing readings blank. Missing values are never silently imputed.

The MLP was trained and evaluated using generated synthetic data only. Its score is an uncalibrated synthetic-pattern similarity score, not a probability of illness or a medical-risk estimate. It has not been validated using real astronaut telemetry or clinical data.

For offline use, the Service Worker caches the application shell, Mission Replay interface, local model bundle and verified OSD-575 source files after an initial successful online load. No external inference API is required for Mission Replay. External links and resources that have not been cached still require an internet connection.

The project uses HTML, CSS, JavaScript, Python, NumPy, scikit-learn, Node.js, GitHub Actions and GitHub Pages. The browser application has no third-party JavaScript runtime dependency.

ASTRA's main contribution is its evidence-first approach: it preserves data provenance, distinguishes real research from simulation, exposes limitations and refuses to infer when required telemetry is missing. It is an independent student prototype, not a validated medical device or an official NASA product.
